dek: Rezaei said no enriched uranium will leave Iran; presented as Iran's red line in US negotiations.

sections.what_happened: Rezaei said no enriched uranium will leave Iran; presented as Iran's red line in US negotiations.
sections.what_verified: Gulf News reports 'according to Iranian state television and multiple outlets'; X post cited; consistent with Pezeshkian's 'no talks until pressure/threats/sanctions lifted' (0600-02) and Reuters 'not preparing for a deal' exclusive.
sections.what_disputed: None on the statement itself; the underlying US demand (uranium removal) is Washington's position, not confirmed by an official US statement in this window.
sections.why_matters: Iran draws the red line: not one gram leaves — the nuclear card stays on Tehran's table until the blockade and sanctions lift.
sections.context: Background: Iran nuclear — NEW (Tuesday): SNSC secretary Mohsen Rezaei: 'Not a single gram of enriched uranium will be removed from Iran' — X post + Iranian state TV, speaking to visiting Pakistani Army Chief Asim Munir; described enriched material as 'a major asset and national wealth' for domestic use; rejects a key potential US demand

totw_analysis: Our read: Iran draws the red line: not one gram leaves — the nuclear card stays on Tehran's table until the blockade and sanctions lift. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Should zero uranium leave Iran — sovereignty over nuclear material, or a non-starter that kills the deal?
